title: How to organize the primary media zone | Family Room
description:
Hold the television, consoles, and controllers so anyone in the house can start watching or playing without hunting for a remote.

This is the Primary Media Zone in the Family Room. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One console per shelf with its own controllers docked beside it, disc cases standing spine out in a single row, every cable labeled at both ends, the power strip off the carpet, and nothing resting on top of a vent slot.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Pull every disc case, spare remote, headset, and loose cable out of the cabinet onto the floor.
Straighten: Give each console its own shelf with the controllers and headset that belong to it, and stand disc cases upright in one row instead of stacking them flat where the bottom four become unreachable.
Shine: Brush the vent slots on each console and the back panel of the television with a vacuum brush head, wipe the controller grips and thumbstick collars with a barely damp cloth, and finish the screen with a dry microfiber cloth only.
Safety: Put your hand on the television and push gently.
Standardize: While the cabinet is open, label both ends of every cable, and tape a small card inside the cabinet door listing which controller and which headset belong to which console.
Sustain: When the credits roll, controllers go back on their dock and remotes into the tray before the television goes off, done by whoever was holding them.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Each console sits alone on its shelf with its matched controllers and headset, the cable card is taped inside the door, and no vent slot is covered.
